page: The Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance engineered for high-concurrency CPU tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features a dedicated AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz across 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via multithreading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Vector extensions are well supported, featuring AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 instruction sets, alongside hardware cryptography capabilities such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory is configured at 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio with 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address, but does not bundle any GPU hardware accelerators. Measured uncached memory throughput achieves 124.41 GB/sec for large block reads and 67.54 GB/sec for writes, delivering sufficient bandwidth to keep the 32 virtual cores supplied with data under heavy load.

Benchmark evaluations reflect solid multi-threaded performance. The instance registers a stress-ng single-core score of 3144.37, placing it in the top 10%, while multi-core stress-ng reaches 100519.25 in the top 25%. Geekbench results present a single-core score of 1875.0 and a multi-core score of 16041.0, with notable strength in software compilation via Clang (41690.0) and ray tracing (50430.0). Synthetic benchmarks report a PassMark CPU score of 51157.15, with strong performance in encryption and physics calculations.

The 2:1 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes the server cost-efficient for compute-heavy parallel workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the 64.0 GB RAM constraint limits feasibility for large-scale in-memory databases or deep neural network model architectures exceeding smaller parameter sizes. The instance is well matched for Clang and C++ compilation pipelines, multi-threaded data compression, microservices orchestration, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. Designed for compute-heavy configurations, it provides 64.0 GB of system memory at a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 500 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage, without GPU accelerators. The CPU features vector optimizations including AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. In benchmarking, the server achieves strong multi-threaded compute results, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 100519.25 and a PassMark CPU score of 51157.15, alongside top-decile stress-ng single-core performance. This balance of high thread density, hardware cryptography, and moderate RAM makes the platform effective for code compilation pipelines, multi-threaded batch processing, containerized microservices, and targeted CPU-based inference workloads.
